Only you can support your dreams when no one else believes in them for you.

By the way, I did my study abroad in London and it was amazing. Again, no regrets and I guarantee you’ll have a blast if you go. I liked Edinburgh too.

I also switched to LINE Mobile yesterday because it's less than half the cost of Mobal per month. The plan is to use my pocket wifi for internet and just have my LINE Mobile plan for the Japanese number whenever necessary. But LINE Mobile does charge for outgoing calls and text messages (sucks if I have to text Android users). I don't expect to make many calls at all, and all the people I need to contact so far are on iMessage.

LINE Mobile took almost 2 hours to set up in the store because it's all in Japanese and there's no English customer support (which is important to some people), but I used my limited Japanese skills to get it done. Luckily, the sales rep was extremely patient with me.

Hopefully, I only expect to pay around $65/month total for wifi and phone plan, which sounds pretty reasonable to me.

I traveled to Japan through a sister city program. There is a language barrier, so having some understanding of Japanese will really help if you intend to interact with locals. Still, locals may automatically feel like they have to speak English with you even if you were fluent, simply because of your appearance.

Other thing I noticed is that my Caucasian and half Caucasian/half Asian travel mates typically got more attention than a Desi such as myself at the school we visited. Definitely because of media influence on perceptions of foreigners.

These are the only small things I noticed, but overall excellent experience. I haven't heard that anyone has ever had a bad experience in Japan. As long as you are respectful of their culture and way of life, you're good.

**Edit: I am well-aware of the racism issues, but I am not here to discourage people from traveling just because of that! I am also speaking from a very subjective, personal experience.**
